source_title: Antiquities of the Southern Indians, particularly of the Georgia tribes, Plate I: Tumuli and Fish-Preserves in the Etowah Valley, Georgia
author: Charles C. Jones Jr.

where.page_or_leaf: Pl. I, facing p. 136; leaf n156

caption_or_quote: List of illustrations: 'PLATE I. (To face page 136.) Tumuli and Fish-Preserves in the Etowah Valley, Georgia.' Text p.137: 'the one designated in the accompanying plan (Plate I) by the letter A'; preface: 'The accompanying plans of mounds were prepared from personal surveys'
shows: Mounds A, B, C and smaller mounds, the moat/ditch G G with reservoirs D D and pond P, Etowah River bank on south/east, north arrow, scale bar
licence_basis: Published 1873 (D. Appleton, New York): public domain in US (pre-1931)
notes: Seen on page image n156. lead_us_mounds.md section C wrongly dropped this book ('woodcuts are artefacts, the only plan is Bartram's chunk-yard'): the book has three site plans in my region (Pl. I Etowah, Pl. IV Ocmulgee, Pl. V Kolomoki). Moat + river are strong fit features. Overlap: Thomas 1894 fig. 180 is 'Plat of Etowah group, copy of Jones's plat, No. 1' (already in pipeline) - Jones's own engraved plate is the cleaner original.

source_title: Antiquities of the Southern Indians, Plate IV: Tumuli on the Ocmulgee River, opposite the City of Macon
author: Charles C. Jones Jr.

where.page_or_leaf: Pl. IV, facing p. 158; leaf n184

caption_or_quote: 'PLATE IV. (To face page 158.) Tumuli on the Ocmulgee River, opposite the City of Macon.' Text p.158: 'Of the mounds on the left bank of the Ocmulgee River, opposite the city of Macon, the largest and most noteworthy (A, Plate IV.)'; p.159: 'Here, in excavating for the new track of the Central Railway'
shows: Ocmulgee River, Macon street grid on the west bank, Central Railroad line(s) crossing, mounds A (Great Temple), B, C, D lettered, north arrow, scale in yards, plus profiles of mounds A, B, C
licence_basis: Published 1873 (D. Appleton, New York): public domain in US (pre-1931)
notes: Seen on page image n184. Street grid + river + railway cut through mound area make this one of the most fittable plans in the region. Mound letters per text: A largest (Great Temple Mound), B 100 ft N, C third (cut by railway), D 400 yds NE.

source_title: Antiquities of the Southern Indians, Plate V: Map showing the Messier Mound (Early County)
author: Charles C. Jones Jr. (survey by Maj. James Audley Maxwell)

where.page_or_leaf: Pl. V, facing p. 168; leaf n198

caption_or_quote: 'PLATE V. (To face page 168.) Mound on Messier's Plantation, in Early County.' Plate legend: 'MAP SHOWING THE MESSIER MOUND'. Text p.166: 'the author requested Major James Audley Maxwell - a well-known and skilful civil engineer - to visit the spot and favor him with an accurate survey'; p.168: 'in connection with the map and profiles (see Plate V.)'
shows: Messier (Kolomoki Mound A) platform mound with hachured slopes, a second mound, Little Colomokee Creek swamp edge to the east, scale; profiles below
licence_basis: Published 1873 (D. Appleton, New York): public domain in US (pre-1931)
notes: Seen on page image n198. Messier mound = Kolomoki Mound A ('twelve miles east of the Chattahoochee River ... valley of the Little Colomokee Creek'). Few features (one big mound + one small + creek), fit will lean on Mound A outline.

source_title: Certain aboriginal remains of the Black Warrior River (JANSP 13), plate 'Mounds near Moundville, Ala.' (survey by Dr. M. G. Miller)
author: Clarence B. Moore

where.page_or_leaf: folding plate after p. 128; leaf n12

caption_or_quote: Plate title: 'MOUNDS NEAR MOUNDVILLE, ALA. Scale in feet ... 1905'. Text p.128: 'We here give a survey of these mounds, prepared at the time of our visit to Moundville by Dr. M. G. Miller'
shows: Black Warrior River bank, mounds A-T lettered with hachured outlines and ramps, ravines/bluff hachures, ridge U, field W, Tuscaloosa/Hale county line (dashed), north arrow, scale 0-500 ft

notes: Seen on page image n12 at 800px. This is the ORIGINAL 1905 Miller survey; the lead lists only the 1907 'Moundville revisited' plan. 20+ mound outlines + ravines = best candidate for the mound-summit matcher. Alternate scan: certainaborigin00moor.

source_title: Mounds in Georgia (Annual Report of the Smithsonian Institution for 1872), figure 'Pyramid of Kolee Mokee, Early Co., Ga., surveyed by James N. Evans, County Surveyor'
author: William McKinley (survey James N. Evans)
caption_or_quote: Figure legend: 'PYRAMID OF KOLEE MOKEE, EARLY CO., GA. Surveyed by James N. Evans, County Surveyor. Scale: 20 chs. to the inch'. Text p.424: 'The following is a representation from actual survey of the position and form of the mounds and earth walls on Kolee Mokee Creek, in Early County, Georgia. They are principally on a plantation now occupied by Mr. A. J. Mercier.'
shows: Pyramid (Mound A, long axis N 10 W) with 'Great Ditch 40 by 20 ft, 400 yds long', Mound No. 2 (S 81 W 14 ch), Mound No. 3 (S 86 W 23 ch), wall/breastwork with two bastions and Mercier's family burial ground, Kolee Mokee Creek on the east, survey bearings in chains, north arrow, scale bar
licence_basis: US federal government work (Smithsonian Annual Report printed by GPO), published 1873: public domain
notes: Seen on page image n432. Compass-and-chain survey with bearings: the mound-to-mound bearings/distances (A->2 S81W 14 ch = 924 ft; 2->3 S86W 23 ch) are a ready set of control relations. Scale 1:15,840. Separate plat of Dry Creek/Walnut Fork mounds on p.427 is a different site.

source_title: The Etowah mounds (American Anthropologist vol. 4 no. 2), Figure 1: general plan of the works
author: Cyrus Thomas
caption_or_quote: 'The general plan of the works, made from these surveys, is given in Figure 1 ... a broad, surrounding ditch, flanked at two points by large excavations, six included and one outside mound'
shows: Etowah River, ditch/moat with excavations r and s, mounds a (with ramp), b, c, e, f, outside mound v, lettered points, north arrow, scale 0-900 ft
notes: Seen on page image n15. Probably the same BAE survey drawing as Thomas 1894 (12th AR) fig. 182 'Plat of the Etowah group (original)', which is already in the pipeline; listed as an alternate, cleaner/rougher copy. Thomas 1894 also has fig. 180 (copy of Jones's plat) and fig. 181 (copy of Whittlesey's figure) - check the pipeline holds all three.

source_title: Ancient Monuments of the Mississippi Valley, Fig. 21: Plan of Ancient Work in Alabama (near Florence)
author: E. G. Squier and E. H. Davis
caption_or_quote: List of cuts: '21. Plan of Ancient Work in Alabama .... 109'. Text p.109: 'An analogous work of some interest, (Fig. 21,) but partially destroyed by the Tennessee river, upon the bank of which it stands, occurs near the town of Florence, in Alabama. It consists of a large mound, hexagonal in form, truncated, and forty-five feet in height'
shows: Hexagonal Mound, curved Embankment (wall) from river to river around it, Tennessee River, Cane Island, High Grounds bluff to the north, north arrow, section a-b
licence_basis: Published 1848 (Smithsonian Contributions to Knowledge vol. 1): public domain in US (pre-1931)
notes: Seen on page image n230. S&D 1848 is already in the pipeline but the name matcher missed it: the caption says 'Alabama', not Florence (Thomas 1891 Catalogue: 'Hexagonal mound surrounded by a wall, on the bank of the Tennessee River near Florence. Figured and described in Anc. Mon., pp. 109, 110'). Schematic small woodcut; wall now gone, so fit leans on mound + river bank. Moore 1915 (tennesseeriver00moorrich p.251-253) describes the mound, no plan.

source_title: Mounds and shell heaps on the west coast of Florida (Annual Report of the Smithsonian Institution for 1883), Map 3: Choctawhachee Bay, Florida
author: S. T. Walker
caption_or_quote: 'MAP 3.-Choctawhachee Bay, Florida.' Text p.860-862: 'let us turn to Choctawhatchee Bay, a map of which is presented ... The first and larger of these two towns was situated on the northern shores of Santa Rosa Sound, where it enters Choctawhatchee Bay ... a large shell heap on the bluffs above the largest spring. This shell heap, which was converted into a fort by the Southern army during the civil war ... About 400 yards nearly due north of this heap ... is the mound in question ... Its estimated height is 25 feet, its length 250 feet'
shows: Choctawhatchee Bay, Santa Rosa Sound (The Narrows), Garnier's Bayou, bayous and points, with symbols for domiciliary mounds (D) and shell heaps; the Fort Walton mound is the D at The Narrows
licence_basis: US federal government work (Smithsonian Annual Report printed by GPO), published 1885: public domain
notes: Seen on page image n908. WEAK: regional locator map (bay-scale), mound is a symbol, not a plan; cannot carry a fit by itself. Text identifies the site (mound 400 yd N of the Civil War shell-heap fort = Camp Walton). Better plan for this site remains Moore 1901 fig. 13 (in lead).

source_title: Archeology of the Florida Gulf Coast (Smithsonian Miscellaneous Collections 113), Map 6: The Fort Walton site, Okaloosa County (Ok-6)
author: Gordon R. Willey
caption_or_quote: 'Map 6.-The Fort Walton site, Okaloosa County (Ok-6).' Map legend: 'Scale in meters (contour intervals estimated)'
shows: Pyramidal (temple) mound, US Highway 98, town streets and blocks, buildings (Indianola Inn), test pits, contour lines, shoreline of Santa Rosa Sound, north arrow, metric scale
licence_basis: US federal government work (Smithsonian Institution / Bureau of American Ethnology publication, 1949): public domain
notes: Seen on page image n109. POST-1931: survey of 1940, published 1949 - public domain as a federal work but outside the project's 'old drawings pre-1931' theme; owner decides whether to admit it. Roads + mound make it very fittable.

source_title: Archeology of the Florida Gulf Coast (Smithsonian Miscellaneous Collections 113), Map 8: The Lake Jackson site, Leon County (Le-1)
author: Gordon R. Willey
caption_or_quote: 'Map 8.-The Lake Jackson site, Leon County (Le-1). The conformation of the mounds is highly stylized.'
shows: Platform mounds with ramps (numbered, incl. mound 6 and low mound 7), old excavations, test pits, a road/fence line across the site, north arrow, metric scale
licence_basis: US federal government work (Smithsonian Institution / Bureau of American Ethnology publication, 1949): public domain

source_title: A preliminary report on archeological explorations at Macon, Ga. (BAE Bulletin 119, Anthropological Papers no. 1), Figure 2: Macon Plateau, detail of archaeological features
author: A. R. Kelly
caption_or_quote: Figure legend: 'MACON PLATEAU. DETAIL OF ARCHAEOLOGICAL FEATURES' (ceremonial earth lodges, house sites, trading post enclosure, Moore's Trail ...). Text p.3: 'The summit of Macon Plateau is the seat of several large mounds, both conical and pyramidal truncates (fig. 2).'
shows: Contour lines with elevations, Mounds A, B, C, D, North/West/Middle Plateau, Central of Georgia Railroad line, Ocmulgee River, pond, wood, earth lodges, trading post enclosure, north arrow
licence_basis: US federal government work (Smithsonian Institution, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 119, GPO 1938): public domain
notes: Seen on page image n23. POST-1931 (1938) - federal PD but outside the pre-1931 theme; owner decides. Contours + railway cut = strong fit features. Fig. 1 (p.3, leaf n22) is a 1 inch = 1 mile key map of the Ocmulgee basin locating Macon Plateau and the Lamar site - locator only.

source_title: The great mound on the Etowah River, Georgia (Annual Report of the Smithsonian Institution for 1881), figs. 1 and 2
author: Charles Whittlesey

where.page_or_leaf: pp. 624-625, fig. 1 (leaf n639) and fig. 2 (leaf n640)

caption_or_quote: Text p.624: 'I was compelled, by bad weather, to make the survey in haste. The bearings were taken with a prismatic compass, the distances measured by pacing, and the elevations obtained with a pocket level.' p.625: 'The body of the mound has an irregular figure, as shown in the plan.'
shows: Fig. 1: Etowah River bend, Old Road, ferry, mounds and ponds (site sketch). Fig. 2: mounds A (with ramp), B, C with hachures, Etowah River bank, section line a-b and profiles
licence_basis: US federal government work (Smithsonian Annual Report printed by GPO), published 1883: public domain
notes: Seen on page images n639-n640. Thomas 1894 fig. 181 is a 'copy of Whittlesey's figure No. 1', so fig. 1 may already be represented in the pipeline; fig. 2 (the A/B/C mound plan) is the new piece. Survey made May 1871. Fig. 3 on p.627 is the 'Indian Fort' stone enclosure 2.5 mi NW - a different site.
